metadata.title: Northern Lights on Civic and Citizenship Education

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The analysis draws on IEA ICCS 2009 and ICCS 2016 data for Nordic countries (Denmark, Finland, Norway, Sweden). For principal questionnaire responses, the study uses the ICCS school weight TOTWGTC, defined as the inverse of the school selection probability (based on school size) and adjusted for non-response, and results are computed in the IEA IDB Analyzer. For student- and teacher-level analyses in other chapters of the volume, the text indicates the use of student weights (TOTWGT/total student weight) and teacher weights, with standard errors computed using jackknife repeated replication (JRR). In the chapter methods shown here, the authors apply complex survey weighting for descriptive percentages and significance testing; they do not report any unweighted ML-style estimation, and the weighting is treated as essential for representativeness.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is an official IEA/OECD technical report or assessment framework. It describes sampling, scaling, and instrument design rather than student-level predictive modeling. Plausible values are therefore not applicable to the document's primary analytic purpose; any missing-data discussion refers to fieldwork or scaling procedures, not a single ML imputation strategy.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Uses ICCS 2016 Nordic country student survey data (grade 9 in Norway; grade 8 in the other Nordic countries) and, where relevant, principal questionnaire data for the same four countries. For Norway, the text specifies that ICCS 2009 included two student samples (grade 8 and grade 9) but the analysis uses the grade 9 sample to align with ICCS 2016. Analyses apply IEA IDB Analyzer with the appropriate total weights (student weight for student outcomes; school weight TOTWGTC for principal outcomes). No additional task-level exclusions are described in the provided excerpt beyond the use of the specified grade samples and the IEA’s standard data quality/representativeness conditions.

data.outcome_summary: This volume chapter set uses IEA ICCS 2009 and ICCS 2016 Nordic data to describe and explain patterns in civic and environmental citizenship. For principal aims (Chapter 3), it uses school-level questionnaire responses with the ICCS school weight TOTWGTC and reports descriptive percentages and 2009–2016 percentage-point changes, with significance assessed via chi-squared tests. For student outcomes (Chapters 5 and 6), it models student-reported civic learning opportunities and civic competence using multilevel regression (two-level structure: students within schools) and factorial ANOVA for environmental citizenship, applying student weights and jackknife repeated replication for standard errors. Civic knowledge is measured using five plausible values with IRT scaling, and the models use Mplus with full information maximum likelihood for missing data. The evidence is cross-sectional, so the authors caution against causal interpretations; moreover, the study emphasizes that unequal access and differential effects can reproduce or mitigate SES-based inequalities.
